subject: Post-call: streaming & concurrency budget alignment for ClearSky pilot
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Miller <ethan.miller@clearsky.ai>, Lina Zhou <lina.zhou@clearsky.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: streaming & concurrency budget alignment for ClearSky pilot

Thanks again for the kickoff call today — appreciated the context on the ClearSky pilot and the traffic shape. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, Ethan/Lina, please correct me.

Call highlights (from our notes):
- Goal: 6-week pilot to validate latency SLO and per-token cost at production-like concurrency.
- Primary UX: streaming token outputs to the web client (progressive results) for analyst workflows.
- Target SLOs you called out: p95 end-to-end token stream latency <= 200ms for median prompt length (~160 tokens).
- Concurrency/traffic: expected 150–250 concurrent active users during business hours; average sustained qps ~18–30, peak bursts up to ~55qps for short windows.
- Typical request: 120–220 tokens generated, temperature 0.6, some requests use function/tool calling for structured outputs.

Performance/cost levers we covered (summary):
- Continuous batching: increases throughput and reduces per-token cost; can add a small batching delay (tradeoff with strict low-latency requirements).
- Prefix/KV caching: large win if many prompts share a fixed system+context prefix (reduces repeated compute).
- Quantization profiles: int8 and 4-bit profiles available; bigger gains in throughput for larger models but may need quality checks.
- Model variants: recommend a streaming-optimized variant for p95 goals and a lower-cost fallback model for high-throughput non-interactive paths.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) We will share a one-page perf matrix and recommended pilot config (attached: ClearSky_pilot_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx + redwood_quant_profiles_overview.pdf).
2) ClearSky: share a 24-hour sample traffic replay or representative prompt set + a short list of 10 critical prompts for quality checks.
3) Redwood: run a small enclosed perf run (non-production cluster) with your sample traffic to validate p95 streaming latency and concurrency behavior — propose window: Fri 07/02 or early next week.
4) Post-run: we’ll share detailed token-level breakdown, estimated unit cost, and suggested canary rollout plan (model routing + fallback).

Open questions we promised to answer:
- How does batching interact with streaming (head-of-line latency)?
- Expected cost delta between int8 vs fp16 for the recommended config.
- Suggested concurrency limits per endpoint for graceful degradation.

Ben/Neha/Marcus — I’ve looped you in for technical review and to coordinate the perf run. Marcus, can you prepare two candidate configs (streaming-first + cost-first) we can propose to ClearSky tomorrow? Ben/Neha, can you weigh in on the telemetry we’ll need from their sample replay (KV cache-hit expectations, avg prompt length distribution)?

Thanks — Priya

Thanks, Priya — this is great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming detail: we use token-by-token streaming in the client with optimistic rendering. We absolutely need the first 40–60 tokens to start within ~120ms in the tail case; the remainder can stream at slightly higher per-token latency as long as the user sees progressive updates.
2) Cache expectations: about 40% of requests will share a company-specific system prompt + a selection of the same metadata fields (so KV/prefix caching should help materially).
3) Quality bar: we can tolerate small quality delta for int8 as long as our critical QA prompts (I’ll send those) remain within acceptable classification/intent accuracy.

We’ll upload a 24-hour trace and a 10-prompt QA pack by EOD tomorrow.

Also — can Redwood supply an example config for the perf run that includes: model variant, quant profile, batch window target, and a suggested probe script? That will help us double-check we’re running the same workload.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Subject: RE: Post-call: streaming & concurrency budget alignment for ClearSky pilot

Quick technical notes to answer the open questions and propose recommended pilot configs. High-level: streaming + batching is feasible but needs careful latency budgeting — here are concrete tradeoffs and numbers from lab runs.

Key tradeoffs:
- Batching window vs head-of-line: a 8–12ms batching window (continuous batching) gives ~30–40% throughput gains at 200ms p95 targets for models in the 7B class. In practice, adding >20ms batching starts to hurt first-token latency on p95.
- Streaming + batching: we can stream while batching if we prioritize first-token dispatch (microbatching). Microbatch approach: immediate flush for the first few tokens (priority path), batch subsequent tokens for throughput. This adds ~5–15ms overhead to later tokens but keeps first-token p95 within target.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching is a high ROI for your 40% reusable-prefix traffic — expect effective compute reduction of 25–45% depending on prefix length. We’ll need representative prompt prefixes to tune.
- Quantization: int8 gives ~1.6–2.0x throughput improvement vs fp16 for the larger variants; 4-bit can be 2.5–3x but has higher QA risk. We recommend int8 for the pilot and running a small A/B on a subset of QA prompts for quality guardrails.

Suggested pilot configs (deliverable: two candidate configs attached in the matrix):
A) Streaming-first (p95-focused)
- Model: redwood-optimized-mistral-7b-stream
- Quant: int8-perf profile
- Batching: microbatching (immediate-first-token flush + 10ms tail batch window)
- Concurrency cap per node: 40 active streams
- Fallback: route to redwood-optimized-mistral-3b for degraded quality but lower cost if cluster CPU/GPU saturates

B) Cost-first (higher throughput, slightly higher tail latency)
- Model: redwood-optimized-mistral-7b-cost
- Quant: int8-aggressive (higher packing)
- Batching: 12ms continuous batching window (no immediate-first-token flush)
- Concurrency cap per node: 60 active streams
- Fallback: fall back to redwood-optimized-mistral-3b-int8 when burst qps > 60

Telemetry we need from ClearSky for the run:
- 24h traffic replay (timestamps, full prompts, system prompt variants)
- Distribution: prompt token length histogram, arrival inter-arrival times, percent streaming vs non-streaming calls
- A short list (10) of QA critical prompts with expected labels for automatic pass/fail

I’ll attach a small probe script (shell + wrk config) and the rough perf matrix to this thread. Priya, once we have the traffic sample we can provision a small cluster and run the test — estimate 4–6 hours to produce results.

-ben
